mutations.because: K1b's rule is that a segment eases with its STARTING stop's easing (a); an ending stop's own override (b) never applies to the segment before it. Reading b's easing instead makes the segment ease with the wrong stop's override, which the linear-override-on-the-starting-stop fixture's first segment (still ease-out-cubic, despite the ending stop declaring "linear") is built to catch.

K-D9 folds two-or-more tracks on one (layer, property) in DECLARATION order. Folding in reverse is invisible for exactly two operands (IEEE-754 multiplication is exactly commutative for a single pair, and the two-dy-track add fixture is likewise order-blind), which is why the float-order fixture uses three opacity tracks (0.1, 0.2, 0.3): folding them in declaration order gives 1*0.1*0.2*0.3 = 0.006000000000000001, and in reverse gives 1*0.3*0.2*0.1 = 0.006 -- a different double in the last bit, which the fixture asserts exactly.
